processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Ingots (50 kg) held at 1423 K for 2 h.
Multidirectionally hot forged in the temperature range 1123–1323 K.
Followed by air cooling (as-forged/air-cooled final state).

structures.overall_structure: Austenite matrix with coarse, dark, elongated ferrite stripes/plates at austenite grain boundaries; long straight parallel plates (annealing twins) cross several austenite grains.

phases_present.morphology: matrix cut by long, straight parallel plates (annealing twins) crossing several austenite grains
coarse, dark, elongated stripes/plates decorating austenite grain boundaries; coarser and larger than ferrite in HN steel

grain_structure.texture: long straight parallel plates (annealing twins) crossing austenite grains

defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: Sulfide inclusions could easily break away from cracks at the inclusion–matrix interface due to weak binding force to the steel matrix; inclusions detected in dimples became the initial point of fracture.

defect_interactions.interaction_type: ferrite at austenite grain boundary / crack initiation
defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: Ferrite precipitated at the grain boundary of the austenite matrix contributes to crack initiation and brittle crack propagation.

interfaces.phase_evolution: Ferrite with long parallel stripes forms at the boundaries of the austenite matrix due to the low precipitation temperature of ferrite; in LN steel the ferrite is coarser and larger than in HN steel.

measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: round tensile specimen: Ø16 mm grip ends of 20 mm length, Ø10 mm gauge section, 50 mm gauge length, R10 fillet, 114 mm overall length
measurement_conditions.other_conditions: tensile speed 3 mm min^-1; universal material testing machine WDW-200

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: Engineering stress-strain curves for LN1, LN2, LN3 (dashed); curves overlap in the elastic/plateau region peaking between 800 and 900 MPa; LN1 and LN2 drop sharply around 50–55% strain, LN3 near 62% strain.

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: Effect of nitrogen addition on mechanical properties (LN vs HN)
comparative_performance.improvement_percentage: HN vs LN: UTS +9 MPa (832.5→841.5 MPa); RA +13 percentage points (57→70%); A +12 percentage points (62.5→74.5%); CVN +49.5 J (81→130.5 J); YS −38 MPa (685→647 MPa).

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: mechanical grinding, corroded with 96 vol% alcohol + 4 vol% nitric acid
characterization_methods.purpose: observe microstructure, grain size, and ferrite area fraction
characterization_methods.key_findings: LN steel: mean grain size 20.5 μm; ferrite area percentage 5.08%; austenite matrix with coarse, elongated ferrite at grain boundaries.

characterization_methods.purpose: observe morphologies and compositions of inclusions
characterization_methods.key_findings: LN dominant inclusions: AlN (polyhedral), Mn(Mg)S (elliptical with smooth edge), and AlN–Mn(Mg)S complex inclusions; sulfide occasionally precipitated on AlN surfaces.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: SEM at 500 magnification, 50 random view fields
characterization_methods.purpose: quantify number and size of inclusions
characterization_methods.key_findings: LN steel: number density 73 mm⁻²; average size 3.435 μm; area ratio 0.212%; NP of inclusions <4 μm = 78%; size distribution 39% (<2 μm), 39% (2–4 μm), 12% (4–6 μm), 10% (>6 μm).

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: room temperature; strain rate 1 × 10^-3 s^-1; tensile speed 3 mm min^-1
characterization_methods.purpose: determine YS, UTS, RA, elongation and stress-strain curves

characterization_methods.technique: SEM and super-depth-of-field microscope fracture surface observation
characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: SEM; super-depth of field microscope VHX-500
characterization_methods.purpose: observe tensile and impact fracture morphologies
characterization_methods.key_findings: LN tensile fracture: fracture section at 45° to load direction; small, shallow equiaxed dimples, smaller in size and greater in number (more severe local stress concentration). LN impact fracture: standard ductile impact fracture with fibrous, radiation and shear lip zones; shear lip area ratio lower than HN; dimples small and elongated in crack propagation direction.

computational_details.software_used: calculation method from previous work; liquidus and solidus calculated using FactSage 8.0
computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Fe–28Mn–10Al–0.8C steel; [Al] (wt%) vs [N] (wt%); smelting temperature 1873 K, liquidus 1587 K, solidus 1493 K
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: LN composition (Al 9.90 wt%, N 0.0025 wt%) plots below the equilibrium line of the smelting temperature, indicating AlN was not stable and could not be generated during smelting.

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Fe–28Mn–10Al–0.8C–N system; temperature 700–1800 K vs mass fraction of nitrogen 0.0–2.0 wt%

unmapped_findings: LN steel chemical composition (Table 1, wt%): Mn 28.21, Al 9.90, C 0.82, N 0.0025, S 0.0085, Fe Bal. [b0015, table_001]
LN steel reduction of area (RA) = 57(±6) % from the room-temperature tensile test (Table 2). [b0029, table_002]
LN steel Charpy impact energy (CVN) = 81(±3) J from the JB-300B impact test (Table 2). [b0029, table_002]

LN steel inclusion statistics: number density 73 mm⁻², average size 3.435 μm, area ratio 0.212%; NP of inclusions <4 μm = 78%; size distribution 39% (<2 μm), 39% (2–4 μm), 12% (4–6 μm), 10% (>6 μm). [b0033, table_003, figure_006]

LN steel tensile fracture: fracture section was 45° to the load direction; the LN sample fractured by shear stress at 45° before the loading-direction stress reached its tensile strength; dimples smaller in size and greater in number. [b0051, b0055, figure_010]

LN steel impact fracture: standard ductile impact fracture including fibrous, radiation and shear lip zones; shear lip zone area ratio lower than in HN steel; dimples small and elongated in the crack propagation direction, greatly affected by shear force, accelerating crack propagation. [b0059, figure_011]

AlN stability for LN steel: the Al (9.90 wt%) and N (0.0025 wt%) composition fell below the equilibrium line of the smelting temperature (1873 K), indicating AlN was not a stable phase and could not be generated during smelting. [b0044, figure_008]
Ingots (50 kg) were manufactured using a vacuum medium-frequency induction furnace from pure iron, ferromanganese, carbon particles, aluminum particles, and manganese nitrogen alloy. [b0013]
The LN steel generally broke earlier than the HN steel during local necking in the tensile test; energy consumption of LN fracture is lower than HN fracture. [b0051]

The tensile specimen geometry (figure_001) is Ø16 mm grip ends of 20 mm length, Ø10 mm gauge section, 50 mm gauge length, R10 fillet, 114 mm overall length; the impact specimen is a 50 mm × 10 mm × 10 mm Charpy-type bar with a 45° V-notch, 2 mm notch depth and 8 mm remaining ligament. [figure_001]
